entities.summary: Count Gustaf Mauritz Armfelt was a Finnish-Swedish count, baron, courtier, general and diplomat who played a crucial role in shaping the Russian Empire's Finnish governorate from 1809 to 1812. Born into the noble family of the nobility in Finland, Armfelt was educated in the military and diplomatic arts, eventually joining the Russian imperial service. He rose through the ranks, becoming a trusted advisor to Tsar Alexander I, and was instrumental in the creation of the Finnish Senate, a central institution in the governance of Finland during the Russian era. Armfelt's legacy extends to the modern-day Republic of Finland, where he is remembered as a key figure in the country's history and a symbol of the complex and often fraught relationship between Finland and Russia. The Finnish historian, Lars-Göran Larsson, once wrote, 'Gustaf Mauritz Armfelt was the first of the Finns to hold the position of Governor General of Finland, a position that would later become a key element in the country's struggle for autonomy.'
